title: US grants Aurora exemption for self-driving trucks safety feature
source_used: Reuters (text read on SRN News, which carries the Reuters report with its byline; the Reuters page returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: The US transport department approved a five-year exemption for Aurora and other self-driving truck companies from rules that require drivers to place warning devices around a stopped truck.
Trucks may use warning beacons mounted on the cab instead; the department says this gives an equal or greater level of safety.
Companies must notify the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration beforehand and disclose crashes involving a vehicle while its beacons are on or should have been on.
The agency says it would revoke an exemption if it lowers safety below earlier levels.
Aurora has about 20 self-driving trucks in on-road operations and filed a new five-year application in April.
Aurora sued the agency in early 2025 and dropped the suit after a temporary three-month waiver issued in October 2025.
quote_evidence: The US transportation department said late on Wednesday it approved a five-year exemption for Aurora and other self-driving trucking companies from rules that require drivers to place warning devices around a stopped truck.
The agency said it would revoke exemptions if it results in a lower level of safety than was maintained before it was granted.
why_it_matters_hint: Self-driving trucks gain a legal route past a rule written for human drivers.
notes: Byline on the Reuters text: Reuters reporter David Shepardson. NTD News carries a shorter copy. The Reuters link in the entry is unread (HTTP 401 here).
